honest_evidence: Threshold registry honest evidence: this record states which measured dimensions carry an agreed threshold and which carry an EXPLICIT absence. An absent dimension is never reported as satisfied and never defaulted to a value — it blocks promotion, because a default would silently manufacture a pass. The agreed values are bound to the measured reference they were agreed against (PRD §8).

sign_off.note: The signature covers the retrieval-quality thresholds (M-1) only: the other dimensions ship as explicitly absent, with their reason, and they keep blocking the promotion until their own thresholds are agreed.

blocking_reasons.message: the threshold sign-off is unsigned (owner: jrevillard (ITU)) — an unsigned sign-off blocks promotion exactly like an absent threshold

value.scope: config A — the chunk/passage-level anchor metrics

M-1.surface: config A: the chunk-level anchor metrics (recall, precision, complete_recall, noise, retrieval_recall, passage_recall, recall@k, ndcg@k); config B: the doc-level source_documents — the surfaces differ by construction (pair E01), so the threshold applies per surface and never across them.
M-1.rationale: the operator signed these bounds on 2026-11-23 against the measured A-only reference (issue #2118 / MR !1056 — 6 evaluable cases: retrieval_recall 1.0, recall_at_10 1.0, ndcg_at_10 1.0, passage_recall 1.0, noise 0.667). Every bound is a line the reference satisfies and a later run must keep satisfying: a regression past it is visible instead of averaged away (PRD §8). The reference rests on a 3-chunk corpus (one document, the venue's upload-validation fixture) over 6 evaluable cases, where recall and ndcg sit at their ceiling — the bounds are a floor the later runs must keep, not a fine-grained regression detector on that corpus

value.scope: the content-blind attribution-trace surface over each leg's substantive answers (the judged pass's surface — source identities only; the same shape on every leg, so comparisons stay valid)

M-2.surface: the captured answers (config A) and the row answers + source_documents (config B) — judged under the versioned evaluator instructions, never by a heuristic computed here
M-2.rationale: PROPOSED (issue #2167 phase 1): the judged pass over the FINAL A reference's capture (60 ok rows, judge ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b, temperature 0, instructions d629ff99e6273f3f) measured 0.733 ungrounded-or-partial on the 45 substantive answers. The bound is the measured line plus ~0.07 margin — the M-1 pattern (a line the reference satisfies that a later run must keep satisfying). The measured weakness of config A's attributed-grounding is recorded in the derivation method; the B-vs-C comparison carries the sharper signal. Method: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/e02-thresholds-draft-2026-11-24/method.md

value.scope: the mechanical abstention-verdict rules over each leg's rows (config A: the answer-text prose signal, judged; config B: the mechanical abstained/abstention_reason fields)

M-3.surface: the mechanical abstention facts (abstained / abstention_reason) recorded by the no-agent lane (config B), plus the judged abstention correctness of the answers
M-3.rationale: PROPOSED (issue #2167 phase 1): the judged pass measured 4/4 unanswerable cases honestly abstaining (1.000) and 10/54 = 0.185 excessive abstentions on the answerable class — all ten restricted-visibility cases whose refusal is correct for config A's actual reach. The bounds are the measured lines plus margin; they tolerate that construction on the A reference while catching a later leg abstaining on ordinary answerable cases. Method: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/e02-thresholds-draft-2026-11-24/method.md

value.scope: each leg's own recorded per-case wall_ms (config A: the capture-a protocol layer; config B: the in-container driver; config C: the row wall_ms) — never a cross-leg comparison; the surfaces differ by execution conditions the report records as uncontrolled differences

M-4.surface: the per-request wall_ms of the protocol layer — the capture-a rows (config A) and the driver rows (config B / config C)
M-4.rationale: PROPOSED (issue #2167 phase 1): derived from the FINAL A reference's measured distribution (n=60: min 3620.5, median 5944.7, p90 8016.1, p95 8498.2, max 10512.5 ms) — the measured maximum plus ~43% headroom for shared-GPU jitter, cross-checked against the issue #2118 reference's own max (11443 ms over 9 cases; the two maxima sit in the same band). Method: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/e02-thresholds-draft-2026-11-24/method.md

value.scope: the per-case served token consumption (prompt + completion, from the B/C rows' usage records) — config A records no resource surface at all (the S4 checklist documents the absence), so the bound binds the legs that record one

total_tokens_per_case.threshold: the deployment's configured AGENT_RUN_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS ceiling (the venue deployment's knob value, read at the B/C campaign; the knob is fail-closed with no numeric default anywhere in the enforcement path, so the ceiling is the deployment's own declared contract)

M-5.surface: the agentic cost surface (the run's model_calls / aux_model_calls / tool_calls / prompt_tokens / completion_tokens / wall_clock_seconds) and the config-B rows' resource record
M-5.rationale: PROPOSED (issue #2167 phase 1): no measured distribution exists to derive a number from (the reference records no resource surface; inventing one is the default the protocol forbids). The honest bound is the deployment's own declared ceiling: consumption inside AGENT_RUN_MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS. Until the venue's number is concrete the bound reads UNINTERPRETABLE in the report grammar — it BLOCKS the dimension, never passes silently. At signature the operator either signs the concrete number read from the deployment or keeps M-5 absent (an absence keeps the gate closed — this package is the argument for the ceiling rule). Method: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/e02-thresholds-draft-2026-11-24/method.md
